What is eaten, when it is eaten, and what eating it says.

**19 customs, around 14 dishes.** What this world eats, and -- the part that matters -- when and why.

**The customs are the reason this page exists.** A `foodway` is deliberately not exported to the game: what a loaf *means* on the night the river comes over the bank is a fact about a people and belongs beside mythology. The dishes themselves are the game's to cook, and live there.

## What is eaten, and what it is for

### Item_choddo_shak

> **The Fourteen** *(harappan)* -- The last night before the dark of the year, when the household eats fourteen bitter greens.
>
> That the year has a worst night and everyone gets through it together. The greens are gathered that morning from ditch, bund, pond and field edge -- most of them things nobody planted, and several that are only food because somebody once had to find out. It is a meal about having survived a season of not much, eaten deliberately while there is still not much.
>
> **Fourteen is the whole of it.** Which fourteen shifts from household to household and from the delta to the plateau, and nobody argues about the list; a cook one short goes back out rather than making it with thirteen. The count is the observance and the plants are what happened to be growing.

### Item_date_block

> **The parting block** *(trader)* -- Pressed into the hands of someone leaving on a crossing.
>
> You are expected back. Refusing one is how you say you are not coming.

> **The palm's return** *(harappan)* -- Left at the foot of the tree it came from, at the end of the harvest.
>
> The palm is owed something. A practical culture doing an impractical thing, which is usually where a foodway is.

### Item_dried_fish

> **The weir's share** *(harappan)* -- Whenever a weir is lifted, before anything is counted.
>
> The first rack goes to whoever did not fish that day. A weir catches without effort, so the catch is treated as luck rather than as work.

> **The desert ration** *(trader)* -- Counted out by the day before a caravan leaves Dwarka.
>
> A crossing is arithmetic. Counting the fish in front of everybody is how a caravan agrees it is possible before it commits.

### Item_flood_bread

> **The rising loaf** *(harappan)* -- The first day the river comes over the bank.
>
> That the flood is a harvest and not a disaster. Taro is the crop that wants the water the rice cannot take, so a loaf stretched with taro is the year saying it will be all right.

> **The thin loaf** *(harappan)* -- A year the flood does not come.
>
> The same loaf, made when the reason for it has failed. Baking it anyway is either stubbornness or a prayer, and canon does not say which.

### Item_green_mango_sour

> **The sour ration** *(trader)* -- Cut and salted before the mangoes ripen, for a crossing later in the year.
>
> Bad water is a fact of a long walk and this is what makes it drinkable. A caravan that has run out is a caravan that turns back, so the sour is counted out at the start beside the dried fish.

### Item_jackfruit_curry

> **The month before sweets** *(harappan)* -- The weeks when the fruit is on the tree and not yet ripe.
>
> The same tree feeds you twice with a month between, and the first time it does not taste like a treat. Eating it green is not making do -- it is knowing the tree well enough to take what it has now instead of waiting for what it will have.

### Item_mahua_liquor

> **The bitter cup** *(jharwa)* -- The night after a burial, and not before.
>
> Grief is drunk at once and in company rather than carried. Drinking it alone is the clearest way in the Jharwa hills to say something is wrong.

> **The struck cup** *(tushara)* -- At the closing of a trade, poured by the seller.
>
> A bargain is not done when the goods move; it is done when both have drunk. The tally stick records it and the cup finishes it.

### Item_neem_salve

> **The bitter mark** *(harappan)* -- Smeared on a newborn, once.
>
> Bitterness first, so nothing after it is a shock. Canon has neem for medicine and this is the reading the delta puts on it.

### Item_salt_fish_stew

> **The common pot** *(harappan)* -- Any evening nobody has marked as anything.
>
> Almost nothing, and that is the point -- a culture is mostly the meal it does not think about.

### Item_shell_bead

> **The counted string** *(harappan)* -- Strung one bead a season from a child's birth, given at their marriage.
>
> Worth measured in patience rather than in quantity. A string bought whole fools nobody, because the beads do not match.

### Item_spiced_oil

> **The last pour** *(harappan)* -- Poured over a dish at the moment it reaches the table, never before.
>
> The smell arrives before the food does, and that is the point: a household with nothing much in the pot can still make the room smell as though it has. It is the most a poor kitchen can do and everybody knows it, which is why nobody says so.

### Item_spiced_rice

> **The set place** *(harappan)* -- Laid for a traveller before they are asked their business.
>
> That hospitality is not a judgement. The question comes after the meal, and asking it first is the insult.

### Item_tamarind_paste

> **The sour season** *(harappan)* -- Through the worst of the heat, in almost everything.
>
> Sour food is how a delta survives its own summer. Nobody calls it a custom; everybody does it.

### Item_travel_cake

> **Vigil cake** *(wanderer)* -- Baked before a journey nobody expects to be short.
>
> It keeps badly as food and perfectly as a promise: the person who baked it expects to eat the last of it somewhere else.

> **The last cake** *(wanderer)* -- Eaten by those who stayed, when someone does not come back.
>
> The promise the vigil cake made, finished by the wrong people. Nothing is said while it is eaten.
